proposition: For a coverage-one binary controller whose only scorable outputs are correct singletons and the full binary envelope, mean harm equals 0.25 times its unresolved/full-envelope rate. Harm noninferiority to comparator harm h therefore requires unresolved_rate <= 4h, equivalently correct_singleton_rate >= 1-4h.
proof: Coverage one excludes wrong singleton outputs. If q is the full-envelope rate, correct singletons contribute zero and full envelopes contribute 0.25, so H=0.25q. H<=h iff q<=4h.
conclusion: The one safe V3 glue cell is scientifically nontrivial but far too sparse for harm noninferiority. On the strictest inherited V3 regime a coverage-one successor would need correct proper singletons on at least 89.919772% of scorable cases, not merely a few high-confidence matches. A successful V4 needs a broadly covering obstruction certificate or substantially stronger source-native evidence, not only a precision-safe positive gate.
boundary: This is a V3-loss arithmetic constraint, not evidence that the threshold is attainable or transports to new families. Family-wise V4 thresholds must be computed from each frozen comparator harm without pooling.
